title: Nettle and Her Wobbly Shadow
markdown:
Nettle the goat was having a most peculiar day. She loved her big green meadow, a wonderful place dotted with bright, happy daisies and bursting with yummy, sweet clover. Munch, munch, munch. But something was… wiggly! And wobbly! And just plain weird! It was her shadow! "Hee hee," she giggled, watching it stretch out long and skinny behind her like a giant, sleepy worm. It tickled her hooves when she wiggled her nose. But then, zoom! She scampered over to a patch of buttercups, feeling very speedy. And guess what? Her shadow… it shrank! It became short and stout, like a tiny little Nettle, tucked right under her feet. "Whoa," she bleated, her fluffy white tail giving a confused twitch. She trotted away from the buttercups, and her shadow… it stretched out long again! "Why are you so tricky?" she grumbled, giving it a playful nudge with her nose. It just wobbled back, as if to say, "I'm right here!" "This is a puzzle," she declared, her little goat brain whirring.

Just then, a little light flickered, like a tiny star dancing near the ground. It was Fable the firefly, doing his speedy, zig-zaggy dance in the air. Blink, blink, blink. He loved to zip and zoom and light up the world. He saw Nettle looking all bewildered, her fuzzy ears flopped down a little. "What's wrong, Nettle?" he buzzed, his voice a cheerful little hum. He landed gently on a tall blade of grass, his glow making the grass sparkle.

"My shadow!" Nettle explained, stamping a little hoof on the soft ground. "It keeps changing size! First, it's as long as a wobbly worm doing a stretch, and then it's as short as a ladybug taking a nap! I don't understand why it plays these silly tricks on me. Is it a mischievous shadow goblin?"

Fable giggled, a tiny, tinkly sound. "Tricks? Oh, Nettle, it's not tricks at all! It's about the light! The big, bright, beautiful light!" He zipped up, up, up towards the enormous, golden sun that was smiling down from the sky. "See? The sun is way up high, like a giant spotlight!" As Fable flew, he shone his own little light, and Nettle watched, her big, curious eyes wide. When Fable was high above, right near the sun, her shadow was small and neat, a perfect little Nettle-shape, right under her hooves. "Whoa," she whispered. It was like her shadow was playing hide-and-seek!

Then, Fable zoomed down, down, down, closer to the edge of the meadow, where the tall flowers grew. He shone his light from there, a little closer to Nettle. "Now look!" he called, his voice full of excitement. And Nettle looked! Her shadow stretched out, long and wavy, like a furry brown river flowing across the green grass. It was so long, it almost reached the big oak tree! "It’s huge," she gasped, wiggling her tail with amazement. "It's like a whole new Nettle, a super-duper long Nettle!"

Nettle started to understand. It wasn't a trick at all, it was a pattern! She trotted towards where Fable was shining his light, and as she got closer, her shadow got shorter and shorter. Then she ran away from the light, back towards the middle of the meadow, and her shadow got longer and longer, stretching out like a happy yawn. "So, it’s the light," she bleated happily, her confusion melting away like ice cream on a sunny day. "When the light is far away and low, my shadow is long. When the light is close and high, my shadow is small." She wiggled her tail with delight. "It’s like the light is painting my shadow on the ground, and I can change the picture by moving!"

Fable twinkled his brightest, a happy beacon in the sunshine. "Exactly! That's how shadows work. They happen when something blocks the light, like you blocking the sunshine. And how big they look depends on where the light is coming from. Isn't that neat?" He did a little loop-de-loop.

Nettle nodded enthusiastically, nibbling a particularly tasty bit of clover. "Super neat! I love that my shadow isn't tricky, it's just… sciencey! And it’s all because of the light!" She looked up at the big, warm sun, then down at her now-short shadow, which she could make long again with just a few steps. "I wonder what else the light can do," she mused, her curious goat eyes sparkling with a brand new idea. "Maybe it can make rainbows? Or help flowers grow even taller?" And Fable the firefly just blinked his happy light, ready for more adventures and more discoveries with his new friend. What other secrets were hiding in plain sight?
characters: Nettle the goat, Fable the firefly
